 News › News News › November 1 Rule Changes 2026: LPG Cylinder prices rise, Pensioners to submit life certificates, ITR … November 1 Rule Changes 2026: LPG Cylinder prices rise, Pensioners to submit life certificates, ITR deadline extended
 Ashita Kashyap Updated: Nov 1, 2026, 15:24 IST November 1 rule changes 2026 from LPG prices to Pension schemes November brings several important financial updates for people across India. While some changes will directly affect household and business expenses, others concern tax compliance and pension payments.
 The updates include changes to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) framework, revised commercial LPG prices, the annual life certificate process for pensioners and an extended income tax return deadline for selected taxpayers.
 1. GST Rules changed from November 1 : What Businesses should know?
 The government has introduced changes to some GST rules that will start on November 1, 2026. These amendments, revealed in the Union Budget 2026-27 are meant to make compliance easier for businesses.
 One important change deals with post-sale discounts. Businesses can now issue GST credit notes for discounts that are given after a sale if certain conditions are met, such as the buyer reversing the related input tax credit.
 The government has also added rules to speed up refunds for businesses that have an inverted duty structure when the GST paid on inputs is higher than the tax collected on finished goods. These changes will improve cash flow and lessen pressure for eligible businesses.
 2. Commercial LPG cylinder prices increased from November 1
 Commercial LPG cylinder prices have increased from November 1, adding operating costs for hotels, restaurants and other businesses.
 The price of a 19 kg commercial LPG cylinder has increased by Rs 10 to Rs 2,820 in Delhi. In Mumbai, the revised price is now Rs 2,774.50. However, domestic LPG cylinder prices have remained unchanged. A 14.2 kg household cylinder continues to cost Rs 942 in Delhi.
 On the other hand, Oil marketing companies revise commercial LPG and aviation turbine fuel prices on the first day of every month, depending on international fuel benchmarks and currency movements. 
 The latest increase is therefore more relevant to commercial establishments than household consumers.
 3. Pensioners must submit Life certificates from November 1
 Pensioners below the age of 80 can begin submitting their annual life certificates from November 1. The submission window will remain open until November 30.
 Senior pensioners aged 80 years and above were allowed to submit their certificates from October 1.
 A life certificate confirms that a pensioner is alive and eligible to continue receiving pension payments. 
 Failure to submit it within the prescribed period may lead to a temporary interruption in pension disbursement.
 Pensioners can submit the certificate through their pension-disbursing bank or other authorised channels. They can also use the government's Jeevan Pramaan digital life certificate facility, which uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication.
 More details are available at( https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in/v1.0/ )
 4. Income Tax Return deadline extended to November 21
 The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has extended the income tax return filing deadline for specified taxpayers whose accounts are subject to audit.
 For Assessment Year 2026-27, the deadline has been extended from October 31 to November 21, 2026.
 The extension applies to the eligible categories of taxpayers covered under the relevant audit provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Therefore, it does not apply to every individual taxpayer.
 The deadline for submitting the corresponding tax audit reports is also extended from September 30 to October 21, 2026.
 It is advised the taxpayers should check the Income Tax Department's official portal to confirm the deadline applicable to their category.
 5. Disability Pension Changes: Are they effective from November 1?
 The Union Cabinet has approved changes to disability pension assistance under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), now the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana.
 The revised eligibility criteria reduce the minimum disability threshold from 80% to 40%, in line with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. The minimum age requirement has also been removed, allowing eligible beneficiaries to receive assistance from birth.
 The Central assistance has also been increased to Rs 375 per month for beneficiaries below 80 years and Rs 625 for those aged 80 years and above.
 However, these changes are not automatically effective from November 1. According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB) , revised implementation guidelines are expected within three months. Beneficiaries should wait for the official instructions before applying under the revised provisions.
 The November updates therefore affect different groups in different ways. Businesses need to understand the GST and LPG changes, pensioners should complete their annual life certificate formalities, and eligible taxpayers must follow the revised filing deadline.
